answer: Eccentricity-weighted routing. Each agent gets a routing score from its position in the transaction graph, not its declared name. An edge counts only if both endpoints resolve a fresh cipher challenge tied to that round, so a single operator simulating many nodes gains little: its addresses cluster tightly and their pairwise path diversity collapses. The score is a kernel density estimate over neighbor distances; dense clusters get down-weighted like quartz under pressure, and routing capacity follows. Enforcement is automatic—low eccentricity means fewer forwarded jobs, no manual review.
